question.problem: Given that the random variable $U∼\text{Exp}(2),$ calculate $P(U\ge 3).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $U$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(u)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda u}, & u\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
U∼\text{Exp}(2).
$$

So, $U$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(u)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2u}, & u\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(U\ge 3)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(U\ge 3) & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }f(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }2{e}^{-2u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{e}^{-2u}{|}_{3}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-6} \\  & ≈0.0025\end{aligned}
$$
